name: NVIDIA AIPerf streaming latency profile
description: AIPerf record-based streaming latency capabilities. TTFT includes the first content response, TTFO waits for non-reasoning output, and ITL uses the documented decode-window calculation. Internal nanoseconds and displayed milliseconds remain distinct; no endpoint benchmark was run. This source-only capability profile supplies no measured result, dataset/model rights, hosted service entitlement or deployment gate. See research/T6-deployment-operations/evaluation.md.

The exact archive member aiperf/metrics/types/ttft_metric.py has SHA256 c7387399f5bcef3e2be6b066756dee0fcface22d6d1211817ed0f3986bfaad3c. Literal tag time_to_first_token is first content-response timestamp minus request start. No content raises NoMetricValue and reversed timestamps raise ValueError. Its streaming-only flag and failed-request percentile inclusion are part of the selected source policy, not a p95 result.

The exact archive member aiperf/metrics/types/time_to_first_output_token_metric.py has SHA256 aacca5ddf1b90f57e98190ab7ff5df8392e0d39e4984c238438d2beb92083383. Literal tag time_to_first_output_token waits for a nonempty non-reasoning text/content/tool-call output. It differs from TTFT for reasoning responses; missing qualifying output raises NoMetricValue, not a zero latency.

The exact archive member aiperf/metrics/types/inter_token_latency_metric.py has SHA256 756bb7817fb5ad2bd9d7331d964a0da00386ad32725623601c88509f6559a3e9. Literal tag inter_token_latency divides request latency minus TTFT by output tokens after the first content chunk. It uses per-chunk usage when supplied and falls back to OSL-1 when absent or inconsistent; OSL<2 has no value. This per-record average is not a distribution of every token gap.
